messages.author: da2d889d1cc5c83c
messages.subject: Parsing bug
parts:
Hi,

I´m trying to execute the following function: sub("\\s", ".", "Hello There") and getting the following message:

org.renjin.parser.RLexer consumeStringValue
'\s' is an unrecognized escape in a character string
org.renjin.parser.RLexer consumeStringValue
unrecognized escape(s) removed from "\s"

Is that a bug, or did I call it wrong?


Thanks,


Rodrigo

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Parsing bug
parts:
Unfortunately this is normal, or at least not specific to renjin, within a string literal \s is interpreted as an escape sequrence: just as "A\n" is interpreted as a string constant with two characters, for example.

The string literal "\\s" will give you want you want.

If you look at the method call,  I have "\\s": sub ("\\s", ...). Renjin seems to be removing one \ and trying to parse "\s".  This seems to be the bug.

Thanks

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Parsing bug
parts:
Whoops, sorry, responded from a very small mobile screen. :-)

From where are you reading the code? If you are running the code from Java than you have another level of escaping to deal with:

engine.eval("print(sub('\\\\s', '.', 'Hello there'))");

If that's not the case then it would indeed be a bug :-(
